label: Diagram 10
caption: Diagram 10 Bedding for pipes
description: Diagram 10, titled “Bedding for pipes”, shows cross‑sectional drawings of pipes set in trenches. Part a) Rigid pipes presents four cross‑sections in a grid. Top left, “Class D: Bedding factor 1.1”, notes “High standard of workmanship required” and “Not to be used unless accurate hand trimming by shovel is possible”, with a 150mm dimension to the grey fill above the pipe. Top right, “Class N: Bedding factor 1.1”, notes “Where accurate hand trimming is not possible Class N is an alternative to Class D”, with 150mm and 100mm dimensions. Bottom left, “Class F: Bedding factor 1.5”, “Generally suitable for all soil conditions”, 150mm and 100mm, a “45° min.” base angle and “See Note 2”. Bottom right, “Class B: Bedding factor 1.9”, “Generally suitable in all soil conditions” and “Granular fill to half depth of pipe”, 150mm and 100mm. Part b) Flexible pipes shows two cross‑sections, a rectangular one and a “Detail for vee trench”, each marked 300mm, 100mm and 100mm with “See Key 3”. A Key below defines three numbered fill symbols: 1, a grey swatch for selected fill, free from stones larger than 40mm, lumps of clay over 100mm, timber, frozen material, vegetable matter; 2, a stippled swatch for granular material, which for rigid pipes should conform to BS EN 1610 Annex B Table B.15 and be single size material or graded material from 5mm up to a maximum size of 10mm for 100mm pipes, 14mm for 150mm pipes, 20mm for pipes from 150mm up to 600mm diameter and 40mm for pipes more than 600mm diameter, with a compaction fraction maximum of 0.3 for class N or B and 0.15 for class F; and 3, a blank swatch for selected fill or granular fill free from stones larger than 40mm. Four Notes follow: Note 1, provision may be required to prevent groundwater flow in trenches with class N, F or B type bedding; Note 2, where the pipe has sockets and Class D bedding is used, holes which should be as short as is practicable should be prepared in the trench bottom to give a clearance of 50mm beneath the socket; Note 3, where the pipe has sockets and Class F or N bedding is used, the sockets should be not less than 50mm above the floor of the trench; and Note 4, all dimensions are in mm.
